title: Schedule of Timeframes: Collections Holds, Reapplication and Appeals (Patient Hardship Discount Program)
content:
Three timeframes of the Patient Hardship Discount Program are fixed per level by the business office: the hold on collections while an application is pending, the wait before a new income-tested application after a denial for income above the limit, and the time allowed for a written appeal of a denial.

## Timeframes by level

| Level | Balances held from collections while the application is pending | Longest hold, calendar days | Calendar days after a denial for income above the limit before a new income-tested application is accepted | Calendar days after a denial within which the applicant may appeal in writing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hardship Discount Level 1 (25%) | Yes | 60 | 90 | 30 |
| Hardship Discount Level 2 (50%) | Yes | 60 | 90 | 30 |
| Hardship Discount Level 3 (75%) | Yes | 60 | 90 | 30 |
| Hardship Discount Level 4 (100%) | Yes | 60 | 90 | 30 |
| Catastrophic Medical Hardship | Yes | 60 | 90 | 30 |
| Presumptive Eligibility Discount | Yes | 60 | 30 | 30 |

## Definitions

- **Held from collections** — whether the patient's balances are held from collections while the application is pending.
- **Longest hold** — the maximum number of calendar days that hold lasts.
- **Reapplication wait** — the number of calendar days after a denial for income above the limit before a new application at an income-tested level is accepted.
- **Appeal window** — the number of calendar days after a denial within which the applicant may appeal in writing.

## Figures side by side

All six levels hold balances from collections for at most 60 calendar days while an application is pending and allow 30 calendar days for a written appeal. The reapplication wait is 90 calendar days at Hardship Discount Level 1 (25%) through Level 4 (100%) and at Catastrophic Medical Hardship, and 30 calendar days at the Presumptive Eligibility Discount.
